title: Fatal Frame III: The Tormented
subtitle: Grief opens a door during sleep

body: Fatal Frame III: The Tormented is Tecmo's PlayStation 2 survival-horror game, first released in Japan on 28 July 2005. Rei Kurosawa, Miku Hinasaki and Kei Amakura are drawn towards the Manor of Sleep after losing people close to them. Their connected experiences place a haunted dream beside the apparently safer spaces of ordinary life. The Camera Obscura returns as the means of confronting hostile spirits, making the player look directly at what is approaching. The third game builds its fear around the possibility that returning home or waking up may not fully end the encounter.

Exploration uses fixed third-person views, while raising the Camera Obscura shifts attention into a first-person frame. The player must judge when a spirit is close enough for an effective photograph without waiting until it can strike. Different protagonists bring different strengths and limitations into the manor, changing how a familiar danger can be approached. The camera makes defence inseparable from observation. Looking away may feel safer, but the useful action requires holding the threat within the frame and committing to the shot at a moment when its presence is increasingly difficult to ignore.

Makoto Shibata returned as director and Keisuke Kikuchi as producer, with Ayako Toyoda composing and Tsuki Amano supplying the theme song. Shibata's nightmares helped shape the emphasis on horror emerging from familiar surroundings. The game was planned as the series' final PlayStation 2 entry and reached North America in 2005 and Europe in 2006, where it was called Project Zero 3. Reviews praised its atmosphere and story. Its central relationship between mourning, dreams and the home gives the recurring camera mechanic another emotional context, making the danger persist beyond the mansion's immediate walls.
